4.need-data: This stage uses your data and stages 1, 2 and 3: load it and complete them first.
4.no-findings: The target from stage 2 could not be read in this file. Go back to stage 2 and check your choice.
4.computing: Computing over your rows… with a large file it can take a few seconds.

bet.intro: Before seeing anything: which columns do you think leak the outcome, meaning they carry information you wouldn't have at the moment of deciding? Once you see what the app found, your bet is locked: that way the comparison shows you where it slips past you.

mode.some: Yes, I mark the ones I think

pick.legend: Columns you think leak the outcome
pick.help: {count} marked. Mark the ones you think are filled in, or known, after the outcome.
pick.help_one: {count} marked. Mark the ones you think are filled in, or known, after the outcome.

why-off.some: Mark at least one column, or choose «none».

bet.locked-none: Your bet is locked: no column leaks the outcome.

reveal.intro: This is what the app found in your data. It looks at one column at a time: it can't see what leaks only in combination with others.

leak.title: Columns that almost guess the outcome
leak.why: A column that almost guesses the outcome on its own is usually something filled in after it happens, or a copy of it. With it, the model would look great on your data and fail in real life.

blank.title: Columns that are only filled in when the outcome happens
blank.item: {columna}: whether it is empty or filled separates the outcome (score {score} out of 1)
blank.why: If a column stays empty until what you want to predict happens (a cancellation date, a closing reason), it doesn't exist at the moment of deciding.

id.title: Columns that look like an identifier
id.item: {columna}: {pct}% of its rows have a distinct value
id.why: An identifier (an order number, an email) is for recognizing rows, not for predicting: the model memorizes it and learns nothing useful for new cases.

dup.title: Repeated rows
dup.rows: Exact copies of another row: {n} of {filas}.
dup.unit: Rows with the same unit at the same moment: {n}.
dup.why: If one copy lands in training and another in testing, the score looks better than it is.

drift.title: Change between periods (drift)
drift.measured: The recent period (from {corte}, {reciente} rows) was compared with the earlier one ({historico} rows).
drift.none: No column changed appreciably between the two periods.
drift.skipped: Could not be measured (too few values in one period): {list}.
drift.why: The PSI compares how values are spread across two periods: below 0.10 is stable, 0.10 to 0.25 moderate and from 0.25 an alert. Those thresholds are an industry convention (Lewis, 1994), not a statistical test; the KS D is informational only.

state.sin-fecha: Not measurable: in stage 2 you didn't pick a date column, and without one there is no «before» or «after».
state.una-fecha: Not measurable: all the rows with a date fall on the same day.
state.fecha-concentrada: Not measurable: more than half the rows fall on the last day, and no earlier period is left to compare against.
state.pocas-filas: Not measurable: with so few rows per period, a small change can't be told apart from chance.

find.none: The app found nothing to flag. That doesn't prove there is no leakage: it only looks at one column at a time.

compare.title: Your bet against what the app found
compare.note: «The app doesn't flag it» doesn't mean «it doesn't leak»: the app looks at one column at a time. And your bet doesn't change: it's what you thought before seeing.
compare.empty: You bet on no column and the app flagged no leaks: they agree.
compare.surprises: Surprises (they leak and you didn't bet on them): {list}.
compare.false: You bet on them and the app doesn't flag them: {list}.

inv.intro: For each column: who or what produces it, whether it exists when you decide, and whether you use it. What is filled in after deciding can't train the model, and neither can what you don't know.
inv.alerts: {count} columns with an alert: answer them one by one.

progress.done: All have a state: use {usar} · exclude {excluir} · don't know {nose}.

inv.alerts_one: 1 column with an alert: answer it on its own.

procedencia.label: Who or what produces it?
procedencia.help: For example: «the salesperson records it when opening the account». Optional.
procedencia.required: Required: it has an alert and you're leaving it on «use».
procedencia.help-alert: For example: «the salesperson records it when opening the account». It is only required if you leave it on «use».

row.momento: When is it filled in, relative to the moment of deciding?

help.despues: It's filled in after deciding: it can only be excluded.
help.nose: If you don't know when it's filled in, it can't train: exclude it or leave it on «don't know».
help.blank: «Use» appears when you say it's filled in before deciding.

auto.despues: {columna}: it's filled in after deciding, so it's excluded.
auto.nose: {columna}: you don't know when it's filled in, so it doesn't train («don't know»).

bulk.title: Answer the columns with no alert in bulk
bulk.desc: These {count} columns have no alert. If they are all filled in before the moment of deciding, you can mark them all as «use» at once. What you declare is recorded in your notebook.
bulk.declare: I declare that these {count} columns are filled in before the moment of deciding.
bulk.done: You marked {count} columns as «use» with your declaration.
bulk.applied: {count} columns marked as «use» with your declaration.
bulk.desc_one: This column has no alert. If it is filled in before the moment of deciding, you can mark it as «use» at once. What you declare is recorded in your notebook.
bulk.declare_one: I declare that this column is filled in before the moment of deciding.
bulk.done_one: You marked 1 column as «use» with your declaration.
bulk.applied_one: 1 column marked as «use» with your declaration.

field.momento: When it's filled in, per column
field.en_bloque: Columns you declared in bulk (filled in before deciding)

check.identificador: Look like an identifier (share of distinct values)
check.duplicados_unidad_momento: Rows with the same unit at the same moment
check.falsas_alarmas: Bet on but not flagged by the app
